note.headline: Equities rally on broad breadth, yields jump, and gold rises anyway
note.standfirst: The S&P 500 closed at 7656.98, up +0.86%, with breadth running 22 advancers to 3 decliners as Treasury yields rose across the curve and the VIX fell to 15.84. Equities rallied against a bond selloff and a firmer gold price, a mix that keeps the desk's risk barometer at a neutral 0.32 rather than confirming a clean risk-on move.
takeaways: The S&P 500 rose +0.86% to 7656.98 on breadth of 22 advancers to 3 decliners, yet the risk barometer held at a neutral 0.32 because credit and gold pulled the other way.
Treasury yields rose across the curve, with the 2-year up 13bp to 4.56% and the 10-year up 12bp to 4.95%, while the 2s10s spread narrowed 1bp to 39bp.
Gold rose +0.58% to 4390 even as the 10-year real yield climbed 9bp to 2.55%, a pairing that argues the rally in havens has its own logic.
China led Asia lower, with the CSI300 down 3.60% and the Hang Seng down 1.27%, while every major European index closed higher.
note.desk_view:
The tape looks like risk-on. The advancer count ran 22 to 3, the Russell 2000 added +0.45%, and the VIX fell -11.21% to 15.84. Copper rose +1.39% and Bitcoin added +1.03%, both of which pushed the desk's risk barometer higher. But the score only reached 0.32, still labeled neutral, because gold added +0.58%, EM sovereign debt fell, and both investment grade and high yield slipped. A rally this broad in equities usually drags credit and gold along for the ride. Today it didn't, and that gap is the story.

The bond market did the opposite of confirming the equity move. Yields rose across the curve, the 2-year up 13bp to 4.56%, the 10-year up 12bp to 4.95%, the 30-year up 9bp to 5.37%. The curve flattened on the day, 2s10s down 1bp to 39bp and 5s30s down 5bp to 62bp, because the front end and belly sold off faster than the long end. Breakevens fell, the 5-year down 6bp to 2.40% and the 10-year down 4bp to 2.36%, while the 10-year real yield rose 9bp to 2.55%. That split points to a real-rate driven selloff, not an inflation scare, and it is why gold gained rather than fell. The level to watch is 5.00% on the 10-year. A clean break above it with equities still rising would be the first real test of today's decoupling.
watching: 10-year Treasury yield test of 5.00% after today's close at 4.95%.
Follow-through in China after the CSI300 fell -3.60% and the Hang Seng fell -1.27%.
Whether gold extends its advance if the 10-year real yield pushes past 2.55%.
SKEW at 154.49 against a VIX near 15.84, watch whether the tail bid persists as front vol falls.
note.equities:
All six major US benchmarks closed higher. The S&P 500 added +0.86% to 7656.98, the Nasdaq 100 rose +0.91% to 29368.44, the Dow gained +0.98% to 52573.29, and the Russell 2000 added +0.45% to 2903.94. Breadth confirmed the move: 22 advancers against 3 decliners, a 7.33:1 ratio, with dispersion at 1.07.

Technology led sector performance, XLK up +1.32%, with Industrials (+1.07%) and Communications (+0.99%) close behind. Utilities (-0.31%) and Health Care (-0.18%) were the only sectors in the red. At the stock level, AMD led gainers at +2.49%, followed by Salesforce (+1.94%) and Amazon (+1.94%). UnitedHealth was the weakest large-cap name, down -2.37%, with Oracle down -1.74%.
note.rates:
